title: How flying became everyday: airline passengers carried worldwide and in North America, 1970–2023, the jumbo jet (1970) and the 2020 collapse

sources.title: World Development Indicators: Air transport, passengers carried (IS.AIR.PSGR)
sources.note: 原始提供者：ICAO, Civil Aviation Statistics of the World 與 ICAO staff estimates。以 World Bank API（https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/WLD;NAC/indicator/IS.AIR.PSGR?format=json，lastupdated 2026-10-08）下載 WLD（World）與 NAC（North America）1970–2023 的原始人次，除以 1,000,000 換成百萬人次、四捨五入到小數 1 位；資料集只取 1970、1980、1990、2000、2010、2019、2020、2021、2022、2023 年。2024 年以後尚無數值。

sources.title: Air travel down 60 per cent, as airline industry losses top $370 billion: ICAO (2021-01-15)
sources.note: 只取事實（ICAO 2020 年航空運輸初步統計）

facts.text: The World Bank figures count passengers carried by airlines registered in a country or region, wherever the passengers fly from or to.
Airlines worldwide carried about 310 million passengers in 1970.
Airlines worldwide carried about 4.46 billion passengers in 2019, more than 14 times the 1970 figure.
The world total first passed one billion passengers in 1990, when it reached about 1,025 million.
North American airlines carried about 174 million of the 310 million passengers in 1970, or about 56 percent of the world total.
In 2019 North American airlines carried about 1,020 million passengers, about 23 percent of the world total.
In 2020 the world total fell to about 1.77 billion passengers, roughly 60 percent below 2019.
ICAO said that the 2020 fall brought air travel back to levels last seen in 2003.
In April 2020 the number of passengers was 92 percent lower than in April 2019.
In 2020 international air traffic fell by 74 percent and domestic traffic by 50 percent.
Airlines lost about 370 billion US dollars in 2020.
By 2023 North American airlines carried about 1,030 million passengers, slightly more than in 2019.
In 2023 the world total, about 4.27 billion, was still below the 2019 level.
The sharp fall in air travel in 2020 was caused by the COVID-19 pandemic.
The Boeing 747, the first wide-body 'jumbo jet', entered passenger service with Pan Am on January 22, 1970, flying from New York to London.
The first 747 passenger flight carried 335 passengers and 20 crew members.
The 747 offered more seats at a lower cost, which helped make flying affordable for middle-class travelers.

datasets.note: 原始人次 ÷ 1,000,000，小數 1 位；North America 是 World Bank 的區域彙總（NAC：美國、加拿大、百慕達）

notes: 批次規格建議的資料集 World Bank IS.AIR.PSGR 存在並直接使用（1970–2023）。年份刻意不等距：1970–2010 每十年一點，2019–2023 每年一點，以呈現 2020 年的驟降與恢復；圖表附註要說明。
